events.title: TSX Down Marginally; Oil, Yields Pressure Market Sentiment
events.description: Canadian equities declined Thursday as elevated oil prices and higher bond yields pressured markets. The S&P/TSX Composite Index dropped 0.15%. August retail sales rose 1.3% month-over-month, rebounding from July's 0.7% decline.

events.title: SNB Keeps Rates Steady; Swiss Equities Close Marginally Lower
events.description: Switzerland's SMI benchmark fell 0.11% Thursday as the Swiss National Bank maintained its key interest rate at zero percent amid elevated oil prices and geopolitical tensions. The SNB raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 0.7% from 0.6%.

events.title: European Markets Retreat On Oil Rally, Rate Hike Bets
events.description: European stocks closed lower Thursday amid escalating Middle East tensions and expectations of additional Federal Reserve tightening. Oil prices climbed sharply while bond yields rose, creating headwinds for regional equities.

events.title: U.S. New Home Sales Rebound More Than Expected To Eight-Month High In August
events.description: The Commerce Department released a report on Thursday showing a significant rebound in new home sales in the U.S. in the month of August. The report said new home sales surged by 6.4 percent to an annual rate of 684,000 in August after plunging by 4.3 percent to an upwardly revised rate of 643,000 in July.

events.title: U.S. Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Edge Down To Two-Month Low
events.description: First-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits unexpectedly edged slightly lower in the week ended September 19th, according to a report released by the Labor Department on Thursday. The report said initial jobless claims slipped to 197,000, a decrease of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level of 198,000. Economists had expected jobless claims to rise to 204,000.

events.title: U.S. Weekly Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Edge Slightly Lower
events.description: First-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits unexpectedly edged slightly lower in the week ended September 19th, according to a report released by the Labor Department on Thursday.

events.title: Bay Street Likely To Open Lower
events.description:
Weak metal prices and lower U.S. and Canadian futures point to a lower open on Bay Street Thursday morning. Canadian retail sales data could impact sentiment.

Middle East concerns linger due to a lack of meaningful progress in U.S.-Iran talks.

events.title: Swiss Central Bank Maintains Key Rate
events.description: The Swiss National Bank retained its key interest rate at zero percent as medium-term inflationary pressure increased only slightly since June. Policymakers observed that the monetary policy is appropriate to keep inflation within the range consistent with price stability and supports economic development.

events.title: UK Stocks Mixed In Cautious Trade
events.description: U.K. stocks are turning in a mixed performance on Thursday with investors weighing the Middle East situation and rising oil prices amid a lack of meaningful progress in U.S.-Iran peace talks.

events.title: Swiss Franc Slides After SNB Rate Decision
events.description: The Swiss franc weakened against other major currencies in the European session on Thursday, after the Swiss National Bank retained its key interest rate at zero percent, as widely expected.

events.title: French Stocks Fall As Oil Prices Rise Amid Middle East Tensions
events.description: The French benchmark index fell Thursday as oil prices climbed on Middle East tensions and U.S.-Iran negotiations uncertainty. Brent crude advanced 2% to $105.10 after a 4% Wednesday surge. Key sectors including semiconductors and defense stocks declined.

events.title: Indian Shares Slump As Brent Tops $105
events.description: Indian shares tumbled on Thursday after oil prices rose sharply overnight and U.S. bond yields jumped to their highest levels in nearly two decades, raising concern about India's import bill, inflation and earnings.

events.title: Norges Bank Hikes Key Rate By 25 Bps; Signals Another Hike
events.description: Norges Bank raised its policy rate by a quarter-point on Thursday to bring inflation back to the target and signaled another hike if inflation outlook warrants. The Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Committee decided to hike the policy rate to 4.50 percent from 4.25 percent. The bank had raised the rate by 25 basis points in May.
